A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 21 pages, including figures, tables, equations, references, and Appendices A–F, support comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v4 reports original experiments on LLM forgetting, matrix-completion prediction, and replay-based mitigation, plus Rotated-MNIST experiments in Appendix F.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical studies, including the prediction results in Table 2, replay results in Figure 7, and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The low-rank association models, matrix-completion prediction methods, and online/offline replay procedures in Sections 3–4 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same upstream corpora, fine-tuning tasks, downstream benchmarks, and Rotated-MNIST scenarios. Table 5 revises scores on existing benchmarks without changing coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout. Table 5 retains Before FT, No Replay, Random, and KNN-Offline; the prediction and replay comparisons elsewhere also retain their methods.

E3.justification: Reported training settings, splits, sample sizes, metrics, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Table 5 retains BBH 3-shot normalized accuracy and MUSR/GPQA 0-shot normalized accuracy; no protocol revision accompanies the changed scores.

E4.justification: The model-size analyses, similarity correlations, component interpretations, and overlapping/disjoint Rotated-MNIST analyses are unchanged. Table 5 contains revised benchmark scores, without a new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Single-run forgetting collection, ten repetitions of the prediction experiment, Figure 7's paired t-tests, and Appendix E's z-tests remain unchanged. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 5 revises all four rows in the BBH, MUSR, and GPQA columns. Before FT scores change from 20.27/20.65/14.34 to 37.65/38.31/26.35, respectively. On BBH, KNN-Offline changes from exceeding Random (20.19 versus 20.02) to trailing it (37.49 versus 37.63). These revisions affect a downstream evaluation; MMLU-Pro, IF-Eval, and all other reported results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions of forgetting and association matrices, factorization objectives, and Appendix C's gradient-based approximations are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about low-rank forgetting associations, matrix-completion prediction, and mitigation through targeted replay.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations remain unchanged. Section 4.3 and Appendix D still state that downstream task improvements lack statistical significance, despite the Table 5 score revisions.

D1.justification: Dataset sampling instructions, training hyperparameters, software information, matrix-factorization settings, and replay details in the appendices are unchanged. No implementation or resource-access information is added.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and research positioning in the introduction and related-work section are unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction corrects 'There has been growing a need' to 'There has been a growing need.' The arXiv version/date stamp changes; other prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, table structures, captions, placement, and page layout are retained. Table 5 changes numerical cell contents only, which is assessed under E6.

improvement.justification: Table 5 substantially revises absolute scores and reverses the BBH ordering of KNN-Offline and Random, but the PDFs do not explain the revisions or establish that the new values are more reliable. The main evidence and downstream-significance caveat remain unchanged. The grammar correction offers a small readability benefit, but the overall quality effect of the numerical revisions remains uncertain.
